clue.text: Primer, easy to mix with brush (no hurry)

indicators.note: mixing things stirs them together so their order is lost
'no' says the following word is to be taken out of the one before it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a rush is a hurry; these letters are removed from the brush

explanation.surface: A beginner's guide claims decorating is easy if you take your time with the brush.
explanation.walkthrough: Brush without RUSH leaves just B, which joins EASY in the mix to give ABSEY.
explanation.definitionFit: An absey (ABC) book was an old name for a child's first reading book, an alphabet primer.

clue.text: Murray two up? So one's heard

definitions.note: an adverb phrase: spoken so as to be heard

parts.note: Al Murray is a British comedian, known as the Pub Landlord

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a duo is a pair

explanation.surface: A question about whether the tennis player Andy Murray is leading by two, so the crowd can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: Andy Murray the tennis player springs to mind, and 'two up' to a score; the comedian Al Murray is the one needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak aloud is to speak audibly, in such a way that one is heard.

clue.text: Claptrap about Evangelical Union in Nonconformist venue

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: blah is empty talk, nonsense
the initials of the Evangelical Union

explanation.surface: Nonsense spouted about an evangelical movement inside a dissenting chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Evangelical Union was a Scottish Protestant denomination, so its initials sit naturally in a chapel clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Beulah, a Biblical name for the promised land, was a popular name for Nonconformist chapels in Wales and England.

clue.text: Decisive blow for colonist

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something that settles a fight or argument
second meaning: someone who makes a home in a new land

explanation.surface: A pioneer lands a knockout punch on a colonist.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler is both a crushing argument or blow that ends a matter and a person who settles in a new country.

clue.text: It's famous for its mess (10 letters)

wordplay.note: a stretch of ten consecutive alphabet letters, named by its first and last, read as a three-word phrase

explanation.surface: A note about a place renowned for its disorder, with a letter count added.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like an enumeration but is the wordplay: ten letters of the alphabet run from E to N, read as the words 'E to N'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton mess is a pudding of strawberries, cream and meringue named after Eton College, the English public school.

clue.text: Gritty stuffing for saucisse? Peer wobbled unsteadily under pressure

indicators.note: moving unsteadily is wobbling out of line, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the main letters to be rearranged
P is the abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: A French sausage's filling turns out gritty, and a lord totters while being pressed.
explanation.walkthrough: A saucisse sounds like a French sausage, but it is a long tube of powder used as a fuse in blasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Pebble-powder is coarse-grained gunpowder, the gritty charge packed into a saucisse fuse.

clue.text: Less than what was promised? It certainly involves mother getting upset (12, two words)

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up within, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

indicators.note: upsetting something knocks it over and out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
sure means certainly, of course

explanation.surface: Being shortchanged is something that definitely upsets one's mum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' meaning sex appeal (SA) is a crossword convention; the jumbled MOTHER sits inside SA, then SURE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Short measure is a quantity below what was paid for or promised, as in a short pint.

clue.text: Lateral hair sinks, not fashionable but coiled in knots

'not' removes the word it governs from the one before

parts.note: taken as written
in means fashionable; these letters are removed

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'But' is used in its old sense of 'outside' (as in 'but and ben'), so what is left of the first word goes around the jumbled one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidelocks are long locks of hair worn at the sides of the head, so hair at the side.

clue.text: Bewildered once, having lost last letter in rostrum

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter, so its end is cut off

parts.note: bemad is an obsolete word for driven mad, bewildered

explanation.surface: Someone at a lectern got confused and dropped the final letter of a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks BEMAD as an archaic word; dropping its D leaves BEMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bema is the raised platform in a synagogue or ancient Greek assembly, a speaker's rostrum.

clue.text: One in embassy captivated by angel chimes

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A diplomat is enchanted by heavenly bells.
explanation.definitionFit: An elchi is an ambassador, an old Turkish and Persian word for a member of an embassy.

clue.text: How to address a palm-reader (demented soul)?

parts.note: mad means crazy
âme is French for soul

explanation.surface: A question about the right way to speak to a fortune-teller who seems unhinged.
explanation.walkthrough: The French form of address hints that 'soul' is also French.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the conventional title of a fairground fortune-teller, as in Madame Zara.

clue.text: Hopelessness? Some must accept what's at its centre

indicators.note: accepting something takes it in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: any means some, as in 'have you any?'

indicators.note: only the middle of the word is kept

parts.note: the two central letters of this word

explanation.surface: A despairing question, then a reflection on what lies at the heart of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' does double duty: as ANY, and as the word whose centre is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Anomy (anomie) is a state of social breakdown and alienation, bringing despair.

clue.text: Sow back behind shelter, like piggies?

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

indicators.note: going back means reading the word from its end to its start

parts.note: an elt is a young sow

explanation.surface: A sow retreats behind a windbreak, just like her piglets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sow' looks like a verb about planting, but it is the pig. 'Behind' puts the reversed piece after LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leetle is a jocular form of little, the size of the piggies in the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy'.

clue.text: Foolish Scots greeting stylish vigour

parts.note: an informal greeting
élan is dash or flair

explanation.surface: A daft Scotsman bursts in with a flamboyant hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scots' tells the solver the answer is a Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hielan is the Scots form of Highland, and Chambers also gives it the sense of foolish or naive.

clue.text: It's silly to buy food that makes one feel detached?

indicators.note: silly suggests nonsense, so these words are scrambled into something else

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thinks shopping for groceries is pointless and leaves them feeling disconnected.
explanation.definitionFit: An out-of-body experience is the sensation of floating apart from oneself, a feeling of detachment.

clue.text: Low upwardly mobile Gentlemen will gather in dining quarters

indicators.note: gathering something in holds it inside

parts.note: Messrs is the plural of Mr

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving upward means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Ambitious social climbers of humble origin will assemble in the canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low upwardly mobile' reads as a social class phrase, but 'Low' is a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Mess rooms are where soldiers or sailors eat together, their dining quarters.

clue.text: Herb Mac cultivated, something found on Scottish mount

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scot named Mac grows herbs on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' suggests a hill, but it is a horse; the brecham sits on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A brecham is a Scottish word for a horse's collar, worn by a mount.

clue.text: Tile left in glen

indicators.note: one item sits inside another, so it goes within it

parts.note: a dale is a valley, like a glen
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A tile has been abandoned in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalle is a flagstone or decorative floor tile, from the French for slab.

clue.text: Citrous and glutinous

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tasting of the lime fruit
second meaning: smeared with birdlime, sticky

explanation.walkthrough: Both words sound like a description of one sticky citrus sweet, but each is a separate sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Limy means both like the lime fruit and sticky like birdlime, the gluey substance used to trap birds.

clue.text: Mouldy gems one's included in fare?

definitions.text: Mouldy gems one's included in fare?

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other, inside it

parts.note: cheer is an old word for food and drink, fare

indicators.note: mouldy things have decayed and broken up, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper selling blue-veined cheeses counts these mouldy treasures among the food on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a cheesemonger sells mouldy gems such as Stilton or Roquefort.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheesemonger is a dealer in cheese, whose prize stock includes the blue mouldy varieties.

clue.text: Tiny gal? Quite wrong — colossal

indicators.note: something completely wrong is out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Describing a small girl as huge is completely mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets tiny against colossal.
explanation.definitionFit: Giantly is an old adjective meaning giant-like, enormous in size.

clue.text: I split about relation, regardless

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to rive is to split or tear apart
as in 'with respect to', meaning in relation to

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they broke off a relationship without caring about consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: Respect means relation in the phrase 'with respect to'; the split word wraps it after its first letter, with I in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Irrespective means without taking account of something, just as regardless does.

clue.text: Crew man on dry land, one in bar that is

indicators.note: one item placed in another goes inside it

parts.note: a rod is a bar
a means one
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A sailor ashore is drinking in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crew man on dry land' suggests a sailor ashore; a roadie is road crew for a band.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadie is a member of a touring band's road crew, who travel by land.

clue.text: In Burgundy you must imbibe what's currently seasonal — red or white?

indicators.note: imbibing takes something in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: vous is French for you, and Burgundy is in France
in means in fashion or in season now

explanation.surface: A wine waiter in Burgundy asks which of the season's wines you will drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Burgundy' signals a French word; VOUS takes in IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinous means of or like wine, and red or white names the two main kinds.

clue.text: Tête-à-tête revealing some bits of ana?

parts.note: spans the end of bits, the word of, and the start of ana

explanation.surface: A private chat discloses snippets of gossip, ana being collected anecdotes.
explanation.walkthrough: Ana are collections of sayings or anecdotes about a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête is an S-shaped sofa on which two people sit facing each other.

clue.text: Empty sign on dismantled bus stops

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bus stops' looks like a single noun, but 'stops' is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub is an old sense of to check or stop short, as in snubbing a rope or a horse.

clue.text: It was sub-zero for embattled sailors

definitions.note: the answer is a past participle, frozen

parts.note: taken as written
the Royal Navy, the British sailors

clue.text: Serpent — what figures prominently in Genesis recalled it?

taken as written

clue.text: English despatched in mutinous Meerut, a veteran squad

the letters to be rearranged

clue.text: Drum beaten with a tool, device to vary pitch

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Sort of partition (with reference to fruit)

clue.text: Nurse accompanying a paramilitary force in India

parts.note: a State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade
taken as written

clue.text: Back strain interrupting odd bits of poem, blow for poet
